# safedialer

Source: https://github.com/tiroq/safedialer/blob/main/README.md

# safedialer

safedialer is a small Go library for safer outbound HTTP requests when URLs come from users, agents, webhooks, or other untrusted sources. It validates resolved IP addresses before connecting and can block loopback, private, link-local, metadata, CGNAT, and other internal network ranges.

## Module path

```
github.com/tiroq/safedialer
```

## Install

```bash
go get github.com/tiroq/safedialer@v0.1.0
```

## Threat model

**Connection-level SSRF via DNS rebinding:** an attacker supplies a URL whose hostname resolves — at connection time — to a private or reserved IP address, redirecting the request to internal infrastructure.

safedialer mitigates this by:

1. Resolving the hostname itself (via an injected [Resolver]).
2. Validating every returned IP with `IsPrivateIP`.
3. Dialling the validated IP **directly** (not the hostname), preventing the OS from performing a second DNS lookup and eliminating the validate-then-dial TOCTOU race.

## What safedialer protects

- Loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1)
- RFC 1918 private ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16)
- IPv4 link-local / cloud metadata (169.254.0.0/16)
- CGNAT / RFC 6598 (100.64.0.0/10)
- IPv6 unique-local (fc00::/7), link-local (fe80::/10), unspecified (::/128)
- IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (::ffff:192.168.x.x)
- Unspecified (0.0.0.0/8)

## What safedialer does NOT protect

- Domain/hostname allow-list enforcement (application concern)
- Response body size limits (application concern)
- Content-type validation (application concern)
- TLS certificate validation (handled by the standard library)
- Redirect chains (use a custom CheckRedirect in http.Client)

## Basic usage

```go
import "github.com/tiroq/safedialer"
import "net"

// Create a transport that blocks private IPs when resolving hostnames.
pol := safedialer.Policy{BlockPrivateRanges: true}
transport := safedialer.NewTransport(pol, net.DefaultResolver)

client := &http.Client{Transport: transport}
resp, err := client.Get("https://example.com/api")
```

Or use the convenience constructor:

```go
client := safedialer.NewClient(safedialer.Policy{BlockPrivateRanges: true})
resp, err := client.Get("https://example.com/api")
```

Optional URL pre-check (scheme + port, before dialling):

```go
pol := safedialer.Policy{
    BlockPrivateRanges: true,
    AllowedSchemes:     []string{"http", "https"},
    BlockedPorts:       []int{22, 25, 465, 587},
}
if err := safedialer.CheckURL(rawURL, pol); err != nil {
    // reject early
}
```

## Testing with a fake resolver

Inject a fake `Resolver` to avoid real DNS lookups in unit tests:

```go
type fakeResolver struct{ addrs []net.IPAddr }

func (f *fakeResolver) LookupIPAddr(_ context.Context, _ string) ([]net.IPAddr, error) {
    return f.addrs, nil
}

d := safedialer.NewDialer(safedialer.Policy{BlockPrivateRanges: true}, &fakeResolver{
    addrs: []net.IPAddr{{IP: net.ParseIP("169.254.169.254")}},
})
_, err := d.DialContext(ctx, "tcp", "hostname.example.com:80")
// err != nil — metadata IP is blocked
```

## No chunkbridge dependency

safedialer is a standalone library. It does not import `github.com/tiroq/chunkbridge` or `github.com/tiroq/relaykit`. [chunkbridge](https://github.com/tiroq/chunkbridge) is one example consumer.

## Development

```bash
task fmt         # go fmt ./...
task fmt-check   # fail if any file is not gofmt-clean
task lint        # go vet ./...
task test        # go test ./... -timeout 120s
task test-race   # go test -race ./... -timeout 120s
task check       # fmt-check + lint + test + test-race + guard-no-app-imports
```

# Releasing safedialer

Source: https://github.com/tiroq/safedialer/blob/main/docs/release.md

# Releasing safedialer

Follow this checklist every time a new version is tagged.

## Pre-release checks

Run all checks from the safedialer root:

```bash
# 1. All tests pass (including race detector)
task check

# 2. No unformatted files
gofmt -l .
# Expected: no output

# 3. No chunkbridge or relaykit references in Go source
grep -R --include="*.go" \
  -e "github.com/tiroq/chunkbridge" \
  -e "github.com/tiroq/relaykit" \
  -e "chunkbridge" \
  -e "MaxTransport" \
  -e "platform-api" \
  .
# Expected: no output
```

The `guard-no-app-imports` task (part of `task check`) runs these greps automatically.

## Tag and push

```bash
cd /path/to/safedialer

git tag v0.1.0
git push origin main --tags
```

## Switch chunkbridge from local replace to tagged release

```bash
cd /path/to/chunkbridge

# 1. Edit go.mod — remove the replace directive:
#    replace github.com/tiroq/safedialer => ../safedialer

# 2. Fetch the tagged release and update go.sum
go get github.com/tiroq/safedialer@v0.1.0
go mod tidy

# 3. Verify
task check
CHUNKBRIDGE_SHARED_KEY=testpassphrase go run ./cmd/chunkbridge selftest
```

## Verify the module is accessible

```bash
go list -m github.com/tiroq/safedialer@v0.1.0
# Expected: github.com/tiroq/safedialer v0.1.0
```

## After release

- Update `CHANGELOG.md`: move the `[Unreleased]` section content under the new version heading.
- Open a new `[Unreleased]` section at the top for the next release.
